title: Shabbat Chicken Cacciatore with Bell Peppers, Mushrooms & Herbed Orzo
components_from_title: Tomato-braised chicken thighs with peppers and mushrooms
summary: Tender boneless chicken thighs braised in a tomato, sweet pepper, mushroom and garlic sauce, served over pareve herbed orzo. Cook fully ahead of Shabbat; the saucy chicken stays moist on an approved warming setup. 45 minutes total, 30 minutes active.
ingredients: 2 lb kosher boneless skinless chicken thighs
1 red bell pepper and 1 yellow bell pepper, thinly sliced
1/2 cup kosher-certified dairy-free chicken broth or water
2 tbsp olive oil for chicken and vegetables
1 tsp dried oregano and 1/2 tsp dried basil
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season chicken with salt, pepper and paprika. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Brown chicken in batches for 2–3 minutes per side, then transfer to a plate; it will finish cooking in the sauce.
Add remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, onion, sliced peppers and mushrooms to the skillet. Cook 7–8 minutes until softened. Add garlic, oregano and basil; cook 30 seconds.

Add crushed tomatoes and 1/2 cup broth or water; scrape up browned bits. Return chicken and juices. Cover and simmer gently 15–20 minutes, until the thickest chicken piece reaches 165°F. Uncover for a few minutes if the sauce needs thickening.

While chicken simmers, boil orzo in salted water according to package directions (usually 8–10 minutes). Drain and toss with 1 tbsp olive oil and optional parsley. Keep the orzo separate from the chicken sauce until serving.

Serve the chicken and vegetables with generous spoonfuls of sauce over or beside the orzo. For Shabbat, cook completely before Shabbat, cool/refrigerate promptly if made in advance, and reheat thoroughly before placing on a warming setup that follows your halachic practice. Keep hot foods at or above 140°F for food safety.
child_friendly_modifications: Before adding the cooked chicken back to the tomato sauce, reserve one or two pieces to finish cooking separately in a covered pan with a splash of broth to 165°F. Cut into small bites and serve with plain orzo and a few soft sweet pepper strips. Offer tomato sauce separately for dipping. Chop mushrooms finely if the children dislike their texture.
leftovers: Refrigerate chicken and orzo separately within 2 hours of cooking and use within 3–4 days. Reheat chicken in sauce to 165°F. Shred leftover chicken into a pareve pita with cucumber for Sunday lunch, or serve over rice. For Shabbat, if cooking the day before, chill promptly and reheat thoroughly before Shabbat; use only your customary compliant warming arrangement.
